clue.text: Piece of furniture makes rare present

parts.note: something rare happens only now and then
to present a motion at a meeting is to table it

explanation.surface: A shopper hunts for an unusual piece of furniture to give as a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift noun, but it is the verb used of putting a proposal before a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A small movable stand used now and then, for cups or lamps, is a standard household item of furniture.

clue.text: Backhanded pair of editors with 1,000 pounds between them

parts.note: a pair is two

indicators.note: something placed between two items sits inside the pair, splitting them apart

parts.note: two editors, each abbreviated ED
G stands for a grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: Two newspaper editors split a huge sum, a deal that may cut both ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pair of editors' does double duty: the pair is one piece, and the editors are two, with the grand sitting between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A backhanded compliment carries a hidden sting, so it cuts both ways, like a blade sharpened on each side.

clue.text: Bachelor pad gets a brush

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in degrees
a pad is slang for a place to live, a room

explanation.surface: A single man's flat finally gets swept clean.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-handled sweeping tool with bristles is one kind of household brush.

clue.text: Get up and go to box for safety equipment

parts.note: get-up-and-go is energy or vitality
to box someone is to hit them, to belt them

explanation.surface: An instruction to rouse yourself and fetch a container holding protective gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A buoyant ring thrown to someone in the water keeps them afloat, a classic piece of lifesaving kit.

clue.text: Lustre could be the consequence

indicators.note: the letters before it could be rearranged into something else

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Shine might be what follows from some action, such as polishing.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome or effect that follows from an action is its upshot, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Fat bluebottle, for example, is a not very serious being

parts.note: butter is a fat used in cooking
a bluebottle is a kind of fly

explanation.surface: A plump blowfly is dismissed as a frivolous creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fat bluebottle' reads as one insect, but the adjective is a separate noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A social butterfly is a flighty, frivolous person who flits from one pleasure to the next.

clue.text: Take over when Australian birds go north

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading north means reading upwards, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: flightless birds native to Australia

explanation.surface: A takeover happens when Australian birds migrate north.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume control or responsibility is to take it over, as when someone assumes command.

clue.text: The old starting signal falls without delay

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the moment a hat drops
definitions.meaning: races and fights were once started by dropping a hat, so this is the moment the hat falls
the idiom for doing something instantly

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned starting signal comes down and everyone sets off immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase literally describes the instant a hat drops to start a contest, and idiomatically means instantly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who acts at once, with no hesitation or need for persuasion, is said to act this way idiomatically.

clue.text: Bully lying beside a road with diamonds has a yellow streak

parts.note: to cow someone is to bully them
taken as written
RD is the abbreviation for road
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A thug sprawled by a road, laden with jewels, turns out to be a coward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bully' looks like a noun but works as the verb to cow.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a yellow streak means being cowardly; yellow is the traditional colour of fear and lack of courage.

clue.text: Thrown out of bed to join crowd

parts.note: someone out of bed is up
a set is a group or crowd of people

explanation.surface: Someone is tossed from bed and sent off to mingle with a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thrown out of bed' reads as one phrase; the first word alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thrown by news means being disconcerted or flustered, which is being upset.

clue.text: First-class chaps going back for single woodland plant

parts.note: A is a top grade, first-class

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: chaps are men
single means one

explanation.surface: Top-notch fellows head back for a lone plant growing in the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: The wood anemone is a white spring flower common on woodland floors.

clue.text: The story of a nut cracked by a widow of Moab

indicators.note: a cracked shell is broken apart, so its letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
Ruth the Moabite was a widow in the Old Testament book of Ruth

explanation.surface: A biblical tale about a Moabite widow cracking open a nut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Story' here is the informal word for a fib, as a child might tell.
explanation.definitionFit: A story, in the childish sense, is a lie, and a lie is a falsehood.

clue.text: Ensign positioned east of Santiago

indicators.note: the answer sits at the eastern, right-hand end of the place name, inside it

parts.note: the last four letters of the city

explanation.surface: A naval officer is stationed east of the Chilean capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Iago is the ensign, a junior officer rank, in Shakespeare's Othello.
explanation.definitionFit: In Othello the villain holds the rank of ensign, or ancient, under the Moor's command.

clue.text: Boon companion's choice eggs thus had about noon

parts.note: the choice item is the best

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: one way eggs are cooked
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: A close friend chooses fried eggs at around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay. FRIED goes about N.
explanation.definitionFit: A boon companion is a close, convivial friend, the person one is closest to.

clue.text: Big Jack, the boss, in need of sticky stuff

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in cards
an umbo is the central boss of a shield
size is a gluey wash used to stiffen paper or prime walls

explanation.surface: A large man called Jack, head of the firm, needs some glue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' means the raised knob on a shield, not an employer.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumbo-size goods are extra large, so the compound adjective means big.

clue.text: Bound to change, to be sure

indicators.note: the preceding words are bound to change, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something is certain to alter, that is for sure.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are idioms of certainty, used to concede or affirm that something is true.

clue.text: Musically brisk and organised by Miss Fitzgerald on return

indicators.note: on its return journey the whole sequence comes back in the opposite direction

parts.note: ORG is an abbreviation for organised or organisation
Ella Fitzgerald, the American jazz singer

explanation.surface: A lively musical piece arranged by Ella Fitzgerald for her comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian tempo marking tells players to perform quickly and in a lively manner.

clue.text: Rich cake in advertisement supplied to worker

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: AD is short for advertisement
a bun is a small cake
the worker ant is the standard crossword worker

explanation.surface: A rich cake promoted in an advert is handed to a labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rich in the sense of plentiful or copious, as in a rich supply, means there is plenty.

clue.text: One who punts puts only the last bit of gas in meter

indicators.text: puts only the last bit of
indicators.note: just the final letter of the first word is slipped inside the second, while the rest stays ahead of it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gambler economises by putting only the dregs of gas into the meter.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the final letter of the fuel goes inside; the rest of the word stays in front. To punt is British slang for to bet.
explanation.definitionFit: Punting in British slang is placing a bet, and a gambler or habitual bettor is a gamester.

clue.text: Mournful guru catches bus with oil sprinkled around

indicators.note: things sprinkled around are scattered in no set order, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gloomy spiritual teacher boards a bus that has oil splashed about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lugubrious describes a doleful, gloomy manner, as if in sorrow or grief.

clue.text: Understanding exercise, but still getting flu

parts.note: a grip on something is a firm understanding of it
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Someone who knows to work out still catches flu.
explanation.definitionFit: Grippe is an old word, borrowed from French, for influenza.

clue.text: Insignificant person turns out nicest

indicators.note: turns out suggests the letters are turned over and set out afresh

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A nobody proves to be the kindest of all.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a bug or creepy-crawly is a contemptuous way to label a worthless, contemptible individual.

clue.text: Slugs in the morning need a doctor

parts.note: AM stands for ante meridiem, before noon
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: Garden pests found at dawn call for a physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slugs' looks like garden pests but means bullets.
explanation.definitionFit: Slugs are bullets in slang, and ammo is the casual word for ammunition.

clue.text: Literary gang leader has cigarette at home

parts.note: fag is British slang for a cigarette
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A fictional gangster relaxes with a smoke in his own house.
explanation.definitionFit: In Dickens's Oliver Twist this old villain runs a gang of child pickpockets in London.

clue.text: Stage names include a substitute for Lassie

indicators.note: a substitute replaces the original arrangement with another one

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The famous film collie needed a stand-in, credited under other names.
explanation.walkthrough: Lassie is the collie of film and television, whose role was played by several dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer's stage name is an assumed name, one of the false identities called aliases.

clue.text: Salt lake where cold marine animal loses its tail

indicators.note: an animal that loses its tail is cut short at the back

parts.note: a dead body is cold
a seal lives in the sea

explanation.surface: A salty lake where a chilly sea creature somehow loses its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The salt lake between Israel and Jordan is so saline that almost nothing lives in it.

clue.text: Almost sluggish when capturing the governor in Bolivia

definitions.note: a place in Bolivia, its seat of government

indicators.note: capturing means holding something inside, so one piece goes around the other
almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: sluggish means lazy
governor is slang for father, pa

explanation.surface: A slow-moving official arrests the governor of a Bolivian province.
explanation.walkthrough: LAZ, lazy minus its last letter, wraps around PA. 'The governor' is old British slang for one's father or boss.
explanation.definitionFit: La Paz is Bolivia's seat of government and its best-known city, high in the Andes.

clue.text: Ballad ain't clean when broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, as seed is sown, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A song with crude lyrics gets aired on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantilena is a smooth, lyrical vocal melody or ballad-like song, from the Latin for song.
